stem: Which of these are regulatory signs under the MUTCD? Select the three that apply.

options.text: Curve sign on a yellow diamond

eli5: Regulatory signs give orders you can be ticketed for ignoring. Warning signs give a heads-up. Guide signs help you find your way.
solution:
STOP, YIELD and Speed Limit signs state traffic laws, so they are regulatory.

A curve sign on a yellow diamond is a warning sign. A street name sign is a guide sign.

verify.basis: MUTCD Part 2: Chapter 2B regulatory signs (STOP R1-1, YIELD R1-2, Speed Limit R2-1), Chapter 2C warning signs, Chapter 2D guide signs

stem: Which of these are warning signs under the MUTCD? Select the three that apply.
eli5: The MUTCD sorts signs by function. Warning signs alert drivers to conditions ahead and are mostly yellow diamonds with black legends; pedestrian and school warnings may be fluorescent yellow-green. Regulatory signs state laws and are mostly white rectangles. Guide signs give directions.
solution:
The Curve sign, the Signal Ahead sign and the Pedestrian Crossing sign are all warning signs.

Speed Limit and Do Not Enter are regulatory signs.

verify.basis: MUTCD Part 2, Chapter 2C warning signs (Curve W1-2, Signal Ahead W3-3, Pedestrian Crossing W11-2); Chapter 2B regulatory signs (Speed Limit R2-1, Do Not Enter R5-1)

stem: Which of these are guide signs under the MUTCD? Select the three that apply.
eli5: Regulatory signs give orders you can be ticketed for ignoring. Warning signs give a heads-up. Guide signs help you find your way.
solution:
Guide signs give directions and information: street names, route numbers, destinations and distances.

A No Parking sign states a rule, so it is regulatory. A Stop Ahead sign warns of a condition ahead, so it is a warning sign.

verify.basis: MUTCD Part 2: Chapter 2D guide signs (street name, route and destination signs); Chapter 2B regulatory signs (parking); Chapter 2C warning signs (Stop Ahead W3-1)

stem: A vehicle travels at 50 mph on a -4% grade (negative is downhill). Using a 2.5 s perception-reaction time and a deceleration of 11.2 ft/s^{2}, what is the stopping sight distance?
eli5: Stopping sight distance is reaction distance plus braking distance: 1.47 V t + V^{2} / (30(a / 32.2 ± G)). A downgrade lengthens braking because gravity works against the brakes; an upgrade shortens it.
solution:
Reaction distance = 1.47(50)(2.5) = 183.8 ft.

Braking distance = \frac{50^{2}}{30(\frac{11.2}{32.2} + (-0.04))} = 270.7 ft.

SSD = 454.5 ft.

solution: Space mean speed = \frac{3}{\frac{1}{45} + \frac{1}{50} + \frac{1}{65}} = \frac{3}{0.05761} = 52.08 mph. The arithmetic mean is 53.33 mph.
terms: density
in traffic flow, the number of vehicles per mile of lane

stem: Traffic approaches a stopped queue at a flow of 1,800 veh/h and a density of 30 veh/mi. In the queue the density is 150 veh/mi and the flow is zero. How fast does the back of the queue move upstream?
eli5: The boundary between two traffic states is a shock wave. Its speed is the change in flow divided by the change in density between the states; a negative value means it travels upstream.
solution: Wave speed = \frac{0 - 1,800}{150 - 30} = -15.00 mph, so the back of the queue moves upstream at 15.00 mph.
terms: density
in traffic flow, the number of vehicles per mile of lane

eli5: Crashes prevented = expected crashes without the improvement × crash reduction factor × (ADT after / ADT before). The traffic ratio scales the benefit to the exposure in the period being forecast.
